newsitem.title: UK: EC plans to investigate airlines' over-charging.
newsitem.headline: EC plans to investigate airlines' over-charging.

text.p: The European Commission plans to investigate north European airlines suspected of over-charging in markets where they enjoy a monopoly, an aide to European Commission transport commissioner Neil Kinnock said on Tuesday.
Flexible fares between main European airports "remain a pretty expensive commodity," Philip Lowe, chef de cabinet to Kinnock told a conference on the future of air transport.
"Our analysis shows that fully flexible fares are significantly higher than can be justified by average costs and traffic volumes," he added.

Airlines suspected of these practices would be examined under the "excessive pricing provisions of regulation 2409/92" and where appropriate the commission could prosecute monopoly abuses under Article 86 of the European Union Treaty, Lowe said.
Legal sources said offending airlines could be pursued in the European Court of Justice under existing provisions if the EC wished to adopt a more pro-consumer stance.
Lowe said consumers were "not yet benefitting from lower fares, which on average have only fallen by five percent since 1990, or from greater choice or quality of service."

Despite liberalisation, "there has been no dramatic decrease in fares, no spectacular disappearance of major carriers, no substantial penetration of traditional domestic markets by foreign competitors."

Lowe said that unlike the U.S., all European markets have been historically dominated by a single national airline, and while the percentage of intra-EU routes operated by such duopolies -- one at either end of any given route -- had fallen, it was only to 94 percent from 96 percent.
The percentage of national domestic routes under monopoly control remained at 60 percent, he added.
